text:
anya: Heads up — brought up the int8 quantized variant of gpt-small-v2 in the eval harness this morning and seeing weird metric shifts across runs. main things: BERTScore average down ~3 pts, BLEU swings by 5-8 on small sets, exact-match drops ~2-4% on data shards, and pass@k looks noisy. anyone seen this pattern before?

mike: thanks for flagging. which runner config did you use? same tokenizer, same seed?

anya: same tokenizer, same seed. I used the new quant build: `runner --model gpt-small-v2:int8 --batch 8 --seed 42`. CI job link: https://ci.redwood/tests/quant-eval/1959998887 (artifacts attached). eval-bot: run finished, artifacts at /artifacts/1959998887.

julia: quick check — is BERTScore using float32 casts somewhere? we had a past bug where we truncated before computing IDF-weighting.

sanjay: also check tokenization differences — quant path swapped in a fast-tokenizer shim a while back. small whitespace differences can blow up BLEU.

anya: good call. I diffed tokenizations on a sample: about 0.7% tokens differ (mostly "--" vs " — "). sample: `{"src":"A test — example","tok_old":["A","test","—","example"],"tok_new":["A","test","--","example"]}`.

mike: that could explain BLEU. but BERTScore and EM? could be float precision or cache misalignment. did we accidentally change cache eviction?

anya: I inspected the KV-cache logs — looks fine. But BERTScore code path shows `.numpy().astype(np.float16)` in one branch for quantized runs (see snippet):

```
# from scorer.py
emb = model.embed(text)
if model.is_quantized:
    emb = emb.numpy().astype(np.float16)
score = bertscore(emb, ref_emb)
```

julia: ouch. converting to float16 before computing cosine / IDF will change similarity scale and IDF normalization. that's probably the largest contributor to BERTScore drop.

sanjay: for pass@k noise: are we using the same sampling temperature and beam settings? quant path might fallback to a different sampler implementation.

anya: pass@k config was identical, but I noticed the sampling uses `fast_sample` when `use_fused_kernels` is true — that flag flips for quant images.

mike: actionable checklist: 1) revert float16 cast in scorer for quant runs (compute in float32), 2) normalize tokenization across backends (add tokenization regression test), 3) pin sampler implementation in eval harness so pass@k comparisons are apples-to-apples.

julia: agree. also add a calibration metric (Brier score) smoke to catch distribution shifts — introduced a small pytest that runs on a sample of 200 examples and asserts Brier delta < 0.02 between baselines.

anya: I'll open a PR with fixes + tests. quick prototype patch attached in the job artifacts. PR will include a small script to diff tokenization across runners: `scripts/token-diff --baseline docker://runner:prod --target docker://runner:quant`.

ci-bot: CI job queued: quant-metric-stability-1959998887. Will run unit tests and token-diff.

mike: one more: beware that metrics in CI previously used aggregated rounding to 3 decimals; float16 variability can cause CI flake. Make CI compare with tolerances: abs(a-b) < max(1e-3, 1e-3 * abs(b)).

anya: good — I'll add tolerances to metric assertions. tagging @sanjay to help validate sampler pinning.

sanjay: on it, will run local comparison against the release runner and post results. expect a follow-up by EOD. :thumbsup:

eval-bot: baseline-run 1959000000 vs quant-run 1959998887: BERTScore mean delta -2.97, BLEU delta -6.3, EM delta -2.1, Brier delta +0.012. Artifacts: /artifacts/1959998887/summary.json

anya: thanks — that's consistent. I'll proceed with fixes and small calibration test. updating the ticket: ENG-ML-483.

mike: thanks everyone. if we can get the scorer change + token diff test in today we should be able to re-run smoke CI tomorrow and clear the quant rollout gate.

anya: PR opened: https://git.redwood/p/eng-ml/runner/+/12345 — includes: revert float16 cast, token-diff script, CI tolerances, calibration smoke test. please review.

sanjay: reviewed, left a nit on a comment. overall lgtm.

julia: approved. :rocket:

anya: deploying quant eval again now. will post results when CI finishes.
